title: US wholesale inflation slowed more than expected in July
facts: The US Producer Price Index rose 4.7% in the 12 months ending in July 2026 according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Annual US wholesale inflation slowed from 5.5% in June to 4.7% in July.
Month-over-month US producer prices were unchanged in July after decreasing 0.1% in June.
US producer-level inflation had reached a four-year peak of 5.9% in May.
Wholesale food prices in the United States declined for two consecutive months through July.
Core Producer Price Index, excluding food and energy, rose 0.2% on a monthly basis in July.
The annual Core PPI rate slowed to 4.2% in July, reaching its lowest level in four months.
The July US Consumer Price Index showed annual headline consumer inflation slowed to 3.4%.
Ben Ayers serves as senior economist for Nationwide.
High-performance memory and storage suppliers prioritized data center chips for artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Semiconductor and electronic component manufacturing prices increased 27.1% year-over-year in July.
Semiconductor component price growth eased slightly from an annual rate of 27.7% in June.
The war in Iran caused significant spikes in oil, gas, and commodity prices earlier in the year.
The Producer Price Index tracks price changes received by domestic producers and manufacturers.
Wholesale inflation measures price trends that often precede consumer-level price changes throughout supply chains.
